description.value: Linh Café is a casual French-Vietnamese restaurant in Vancouver's Beach District, tucked under the Granville Bridge at the corner of Pacific and Granville Streets. Chef-owner Tai Nguyen trained at several acclaimed French restaurants in Vancouver before merging his Vietnamese heritage with classical French technique — resulting in a menu that spans salad rolls and pho-adjacent comfort alongside foie gras, steak tartare, and Beef Wellington using locally sourced BC and Alberta ingredients. The restaurant opened in 2014 and relocated to its current Granville Street home in 2021.

No cyclist-specific amenities (bike rack, Wi-Fi, charging, takeout) are mentioned anywhere on the website; the only washroom evidence is OSM toilets=yes, and the menu shows several clearly vegetarian dishes without explicit labeling.
concerns: Location is under the Granville Bridge; website explicitly advises using 'Pacific Street and Granville under bridge' in Google Maps navigation to avoid being routed onto the bridge — cyclists should note this unusual access point.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, actively operating full-service restaurant with a live website, confirmed contact details, and a detailed current menu. A practical dining stop for cyclists riding the False Creek or Seawall routes near the Granville Bridge.
